output.brief: The wrong expiry dates are not an operator problem. From 4 October, every Veltranol job received a shelf life of 36 months from PackBridge instead of 24. That value came from a Regulatory Affairs edit made on 3 October (CC-309). The edit was meant to apply only to lots made from March 2027, but the system applied it immediately. All 47 jobs show no operator overrides, and the printed text matches what PackBridge sent, so the printer and firmware are not the cause. Earlier jobs were correct, so the problem began in October, not before. The site director's plan to remove agency staff would not fix this and would wrongly blame them. I am fairly confident in the cause, but not certain how PackBridge ignored the future start date, and I have not checked other products. Next: hold all Veltranol lots packed since 4 October, correct the ERP shelf-life record and check the valid-from logic with the vendor, add a second-person expiry check, and review the other products changed in October (HX-15-30, MR-05-14 and the rest). Do not switch off the camera checks.
